prompt: Many aspects of the way people dress today are influenced by global fashion trends. How has global fashion become such a strong influence on people's lives? Do you think this is a positive or negative development?
essay:
Global fashion has become an increasingly powerful influence on the way people dress, largely because of the rapid development of digital technology and social media. People across different countries are now exposed to the same styles, celebrities and online personalities, making fashion trends spread more quickly than ever before. In my opinion, this is largely a negative development because it can reduce individuality and encourage people, particularly younger generations, to seek social approval through their appearance.

One major reason global fashion has become so influential is the widespread use of social media platforms. People spend considerable amounts of time scrolling through applications such as TikTok and Instagram, where they are constantly exposed to international trends and influencer culture. In addition, algorithms repeatedly recommend content based on users’ previous interests, which means that similar styles are shown to them again and again. As a result, fashion trends can spread rapidly across national boundaries and become familiar to large numbers of people within a short period of time.

Another important factor is the human desire to fit in socially. Teenagers and young adults are especially vulnerable to peer pressure and are often influenced by what is considered fashionable within their social groups. For example, young people may follow viral clothing trends simply because they want to feel accepted by their peers. Consequently, they may begin to imitate the styles they see online without considering whether these trends genuinely reflect their personal tastes or identities.

I believe this development is negative because excessive conformity can gradually weaken individuality. When people repeatedly follow the same global trends, they may become less willing to experiment with their own style or express their personalities through clothing. Over time, this can result in greater similarity in the way people present themselves and may reduce the diversity that fashion traditionally allows. If individuals increasingly prioritise online approval over genuine self-expression, originality may become less valued.

In conclusion, global fashion has become highly influential because social media and digital technology allow trends to spread rapidly and encourage people to imitate widely accepted styles. Although global fashion can make international trends more accessible, I regard its overall impact as negative because it may undermine individuality and genuine self-expression.
